title: Datahall GPU capacity checklist and on-prem layout (Q4 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working checklist captures physical space, electrical and cooling capacity, and short-term procurement & staging plans for on-prem / colocation GPU pools we intend to spin up in Q4 2026. Focus is on initial 3 datahall pop sites (NA-west, EU-central, AP-sg pilot) with repeatable per-rack constraints for scale.

Status / context:
- Drafted after capacity review on 2025-10-28 and infra roadmap sync 2025-11-02.
- Objective: provision 160 multi-GPU servers (~640 GPUs) distributed across 3 sites by end of Q4 2026, while fitting within colocation power / cooling budgets and on-prem security requirements.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: combine conservative power headroom with modular rack templates for rapid replication.

Key assumptions (high level):
- Preferred accelerator: NVIDIA H100 SXM (nominal server configs using 4x H100 per 2U chassis or 8x within 6U), but variants (A100 80GB or L40s) accepted for compatibility.
- Typical fully loaded single-server peak PDU draw: 6.5 kW (4xH100), sustained 4.8 kW under production with batching and QoS.
- Standard 42U cabinet allocated for compute + network + PDUs. Usable compute U ~36U after network/top-of-rack switches and cable management.
- Colocation power per-cabinet contracted: 30 kW (default target). Where we can get 40 kW /cab, we mark as preferred.
- Chilled water or CRAH capacity must support sensible heat removal equal to electrical kW (1 kW electrical ~ 3412 BTU/h).

Current fleet snapshot (as of 2025-11):
- Hosted & Dedicated pools already using ~1,200 GPUs regionally. On-prem target is supplemental for regulated workloads and capacity spikes.
- Initial on-prem intake target: NA-west 320 GPUs, EU-central 192 GPUs, AP-sg 128 GPUs => total 640 GPUs.

Per-rack template (replicable unit):
- Cabinet: 42U full-height
- Compute servers: 9 x 2U nodes (4x H100 per node) occupying 18U, or alternative layout: 4 x 6U nodes (8x H100) occupying 24U depending on vendor.
- Networking: 2U top-of-rack switches (2 x 1/100Gb redundant)
- PDUs: 2U (redundant A/B feed PDUs)
- Cable / management: 2U
- Reserved spare U for patching: 2U
- Usable compute U: 32U (allows mixed node sizes)

Power calculation examples (per-rack):
- Option A (9 x 2U nodes x 6.5 kW per server peak): peak rack draw = 9 * 6.5 kW = 58.5 kW (exceeds typical colocation). Not acceptable unless cabinet rated 60 kW.
- Option B (9 x 2U nodes but 4.8 kW sustained per server): sustained rack draw = 9 * 4.8 kW = 43.2 kW. Still high.
- Option C (preferred): 6 x 2U nodes (sustained 4.8 kW) + 1 x 6U high-density node (8x H100, sustained 9.6 kW) => sustained rack draw ~ (6*4.8 + 9.6) = 38.4 kW.
- Target contracted power per rack: 30 kW baseline, with 40 kW available in high-density cabinets for 25% of racks (hot racks).

Thermal / cooling requirements (per site):
- Rule of thumb: 1 kW electrical = ~3412 BTU/hr heat.
- NA-west site projected sustained draw (initial phase): 320 GPUs => estimate 80 4-GPU servers => sustained draw ~ 80 * 4.8 kW = 384 kW facility IT load. Chilled water capacity must be >=400 kW to include overhead and margin.
- N+1 CRAC sizing: plan for CRAC capacity = IT load * 1.35 to account for humidity, airflow losses, and spare capacity. For NA-west example => 384 kW * 1.35 = 518 kW CRAC capacity target.
- Airflow guidance: aisles containment preferred. Raised-floor or overhead plenum to be defined per site. We must require containment for any racks with >30 kW contracted power.

Space planning and layout notes:
- Rack density zoning: dedicate a limited set of "hot racks" (max 40 kW) per datahall, cluster them near CRAC supply to simplify airflow containment.
- Minimum aisle width: 1.2 m for front access, 1.8 m for rear & service aisles where heavy maintenance expected.
- Staging & burn-in area: reserve 200 sqft per 100 racks for initial staging and thermal soak testing.

Network and fiber considerations:
- Bandwidth: baseline 2 x 100Gb uplinks per rack (LAG), with headroom for 400Gb aggregation at aggregation layer.
- Latency: direct cross-connect to Redwood backbone is required for NA-west & EU-central; optional for AP-sg on pilot.
- Cabling: recommend pre-terminated trunks to reduce on-site install time.

Procurement & timeline (Q4 2026 target):
- Week 0 (contract signed): finalize power, space SLA with colo and delivery windows.
- Week 2-6: vendor server order and lead-time confirmation (expect 8-12 week lead for H100 SKUs — plan alternate A100/L40 mix).
- Week 10-14: cabinet delivery and PDUs installed.
- Week 12-18: network cross-connects turned up and burn-in of first 2 racks for throughput & thermals.
- Week 16-20: iterative installs to reach target capacity.

Procurement risk & mitigations:
- GPU supply variability: maintain flexible spec to accept A100 or L40 if H100 lead time slips. Create SKU matrix for interchangeability.
- Colo site power constraints: negotiate option for hot-aisle incremental power at fixed premium; reserve 2-4 cabinets in each site rated at 40 kW.
- Cooling failure: bring portable HVAC on contract as contingency for initial burn-in.

Operational playbook (short):
- Install checklist: verify PDU A/B feed, label and map each PDU outlet, run smoke tests on PDUs and network switch, measure inlet temps at 1U increments.
- Thermal acceptance: rack accepted only if inlet temps < 35C at 95th percentile under workload. If higher, adjust airflow/blanking, or move to adjacent CRAC.
- Failure modes: page SRE + on-call colo tech if PDU reading > 85% capacity on any leg for >15 minutes.

Power & PDU mapping example (one cabinet):
- PDU-A (feed A): circuits L1-L8 mapped to server power supplies 1
- PDU-B (feed B): circuits L1-L8 mapped to server power supplies 2
- Configure PDUs to report per-outlet power; integrate into Redwood Console for token-level cost attribution.

Cost estimator (back-of-envelope):
- Servers: 80 4-GPU nodes x $55k =~ $4.4M (H100 configs), fallback A100 nodes ~ $36k each.
- Colo power & space: baseline $2k - $4k / month per cabinet depending on region and kW tier.
- Network: cross-connects and optical ~ $20k site setup + $1k/month recurring.

Open questions / action items (owners):
- Confirm exact GPU SKU mix with Research/MM (owner: Aisha) — due 2025-11-20.
- Negotiate contract power 'burst' clause with colo sales (owner: Marco) — due 2025-12-01.
- Validate CRAC redundancy requirement with SRE/Facility (owner: Danielle) — due 2025-11-15.
- Update console telemetry integration for on-prem PDUs (owner: Owen) — due 2026-01-05.

Notes to self / rough heuristics (working):
- Try to standardize on a per-rack cap where sustained draw <= 30 kW; allow up to 40 kW for <30% of racks in each site.
- Prefer mixing 2U and 6U nodes to provide scheduling flexibility and reduce per-rack peaks.
- Keep spare parts in local storage: 10% server spares, 2 spare PDUs per site, 1 spare ToR switch per 20 racks.

Appendix: quick sizing table (initial phase)
- NA-west: target GPUs=320 => estimated racks = 320 / 32 GPUs per rack = 10 racks (mix-adjusted => plan 12 racks with spares)
- EU-central: target GPUs=192 => estimated racks = 6 racks (plan 7 racks)
- AP-sg: target GPUs=128 => estimated racks = 4 racks (plan 5 racks)

This doc should be iterated with vendor rack density proposals and colo site floor-plans. Put comments in this doc - flag anything that forces more than 40 kW / rack so we can escalate to colo sales and Facilities.
